To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
S6K2 plays an important role in breast cancer cell survival by regulating Akt activation and Bid expression.
S6K2 is an important regulator of cell survival, and that S6K1 has a negative effect on apoptosis, whereas S6K2 has a positive effect on cell death.
the S6K2 protein promotes cell survival in part by activating Akt, which in turn downregulates Bid via p53 to inhibit apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of a kinase called S6K2 (S6 kinase 1) in the control of cancer cell survival.
the role of S6K in the regulation of cell survival and apoptosis.
the role of S6K in cancer cell survival and the mechanism of action of S6K.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S6K2 is an Akt-activating kinase that promotes breast cancer cell viability.
the S6K2 is the key player for the survival of the breast cancer cells and hence, it is an important target for the cancer therapy.
S6K1 promotes cell survival via Akt, whereas S6K2 inhibits Akt activation and promotes cell death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S6K2 promotes cell survival by inhibiting Bid expression via p53.
S6K2 is an important regulator of cell survival and is involved in the regulation of the p53/Bid pathway.
we have shown that S6K2 is an important mediator of Akt survival signaling in breast cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two S6 kinase homologues, 6K1 and 6K2, have distinct functions.
the two S6Ks have opposite roles in cell survival.
S6K2 promotes cancer cell survival by activating Akt and inhibiting p53.
